items.title: Debian permits responsible generative AI use
items.oneliner: Debian chose pragmatic AI governance: generative tools are allowed, but contributors still own quality, legality, and review.

items.title: AI crawlers are hammering kernel infrastructure
items.oneliner: AI scrapers are wasting git.kernel.org CPU by rendering commits instead of cloning repos. Open infrastructure is absorbing the bill.

items.title: Pixel 11 drops hardware memory tagging
items.oneliner: Pixel 11 reportedly loses MTE support, removing one of Android's strongest memory-safety defenses right when exploit chains keep getting cheaper.

items.title: Vibecoding is becoming a security problem
items.oneliner: Cheap app generation is creating more software with plaintext passwords and weak auth. Attackers only need one careless prompt.

items.title: OpenAI distances itself from Cursor acquisition
items.oneliner: OpenAI publicly stepped back after Cursor's SpaceX acquisition, a reminder that AI tooling partnerships are now strategic fault lines.

items.title: Samsung pushes compute into memory
items.oneliner: Samsung's LPDDR5X-PIM hits 614 GB/s internal bandwidth per chip, attacking the memory wall where inference actually stalls.

items.title: Monzo built banking failover across clouds
items.oneliner: Monzo can keep card payments alive during a full AWS outage by failing over critical paths to Google Cloud.

items.title: Rustdoc got dramatically faster in one week
items.oneliner: Rustdoc improved average wall time by 25% and some workloads by 33%, proving developer tooling speed still compounds.

items.title: Virtual iPhones are now scriptable
items.oneliner: vphone-cli turns Apple's Virtualization.framework into one-command virtual iPhones, which could seriously streamline iOS testing pipelines.

items.title: Linux gets a serious iMessage bridge
items.oneliner: Tether brings iMessage, SMS, clipboard sync, and OTP autofill to Linux with mutual TLS, narrowing Apple's continuity moat.
